messages.content: Morgan usually runs 3 miles at a speed of 6 miles per hour. If she runs at a speed of 4 miles per hour instead, how many more minutes will it take her to cover the same distance?

First, find Morgan's usual time to run 3 miles at 6 miles per hour:
\[ \text{usual time} = \frac{3 \text{ miles}}{6 \text{ miles per hour}} = 0.5 \text{ hours} \]

Convert the usual time from hours to minutes:
\[ 0.5 \text{ hours} \times 60 \text{ minutes per hour} = 30 \text{ minutes} \]

Next, find Morgan's new time to run 3 miles at 4 miles per hour:
\[ \text{new time} = \frac{3 \text{ miles}}{4 \text{ miles per hour}} = 0.75 \text{ hours} \]

Convert the new time from hours to minutes:
\[ 0.75 \text{ hours} \times 60 \text{ minutes per hour} = 45 \text{ minutes} \]

Now, find the difference in time:
\[ \text{difference in time} = \text{new time} - \text{usual time} = 45 \text{ minutes} - 30 \text{ minutes} = 15 \text{ minutes} \]

Therefore, it will take Morgan $\boxed{15}$ more minutes to cover the same distance at a speed of 4 miles per hour instead of 6 miles per hour.
